nodes.label: database.Provide() — DI Registration API
nodes.rationale: Single entry-point API: validates config, calls sql.Open, configures connection pool, registers *sql.DB singleton provider into DI container, and registers lifecycle hooks — ensuring consistent setup across all applications.

nodes.label: Database Graceful Shutdown (db.Close)
nodes.rationale: Idempotent db.Close() called in LIFO order during OnStop ensures connection pool is cleanly drained without goroutine leaks or double-close panics.

nodes.label: Database Startup Health Check (PingContext)
nodes.rationale: Pinging the database during OnStart with a configurable timeout ensures the application fails fast if the database is unreachable, preventing a partially-initialized service from receiving traffic.

nodes.label: Application Lifecycle Management
nodes.rationale: Topological startup ordering and LIFO shutdown with automatic rollback on failure ensures deterministic resource management without per-project boilerplate.

nodes.label: Environment Configuration Module (config)
nodes.rationale: Struct-tag based environment variable mapping keeps configuration type-safe without requiring external libraries like Viper, and supports isolated lookup for deterministic testing.

nodes.label: Dependency Graph Validation
nodes.rationale: Fail-fast validation detects cycles, missing dependencies, and duplicate providers before any constructor runs, giving developers immediate actionable errors at startup rather than at runtime.

nodes.label: HTTP Server & REST API Toolkit (httpserver)
nodes.rationale: Built on Go's standard net/http.ServeMux (Go 1.22+) to eliminate third-party router dependencies, reducing the attack surface and keeping the framework zero-dependency.

nodes.label: Explicit Interface Binding (ProvideAs / Bind)
nodes.rationale: Explicit binding (no implicit scanning) keeps dependency wiring visible and auditable. A single underlying singleton is shared between a concrete type and its interface abstraction.

nodes.label: Provider Registry
nodes.rationale: Constructor-based provider registration allows ordinary Go functions to declare their dependencies via parameters, enabling type-safe resolution without code generation or annotations.

nodes.label: User-Managed Driver Policy
nodes.rationale: Injel does not import any database driver into go.mod. Users import their chosen driver (pq, go-sql-driver/mysql, go-sqlite3, etc.) in application code, keeping go.mod lean, avoiding license conflicts (some drivers have CGO or proprietary licenses), and giving users full control over driver versions.

nodes.label: DSN/Password Security in Error Messages
nodes.rationale: DSN/password never appears in error messages or log output, preventing credential leakage through error logging pipelines.

nodes.label: Future: Named Database Providers
nodes.rationale: Named database providers (e.g., primary + replica) are deferred until the DI container supports named bindings. Currently only one *sql.DB singleton is supported per application context.

nodes.label: ADR Option B: Custom database/sql Wrapper
nodes.norm_label: adr option b: custom database/sql wrapper
nodes.rationale: Rejected: forces users to learn a new API instead of standard *sql.DB, breaks compatibility with sql-ecosystem libraries (sqlx, squirrel, bun), and adds unnecessary abstraction.

nodes.label: ADR Option C: Direct database/sql Integration (Chosen)
nodes.norm_label: adr option c: direct database/sql integration (chosen)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because database/sql is a standard library adding no dependency; *sql.DB is familiar to all Go developers; users choose their own driver; naturally compatible with the entire Go SQL ecosystem; core framework remains driver-agnostic.

nodes.label: ADR Option A: GORM or Ent ORM Integration
nodes.norm_label: adr option a: gorm or ent orm integration
nodes.rationale: Rejected: adds heavy external dependency to core framework, violates 'small core, separate modules' principle, locks users into ORM model conventions, and is hard to remove once integrated.

nodes.label: Non-Goals (Spring Boot clone, Java annotations, ORM, Service Mesh)
nodes.norm_label: non-goals (spring boot clone, java annotations, orm, service mesh)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly out of scope: full Spring Boot clone, Java-style annotation processor, microservices platform/service mesh, proprietary ORM, and unverified performance claims.

nodes.label: Spring Boot Inspiration
nodes.rationale: Injel is inspired by Spring Boot's developer experience but deliberately does not clone it. The goal is to reduce boilerplate in Go backend assembly (DI, Config, Lifecycle, HTTP) while maintaining native Go idioms.

nodes.label: Startup-Only Reflection Principle
nodes.rationale: Reflection occurs once during application startup; no reflection on the HTTP request execution path, keeping per-request latency unaffected by the DI framework.

nodes.label: Fail-Fast Design Principle
nodes.rationale: Duplicate providers, missing dependencies, cycles, and route conflicts are detected before the application serves any request, making errors immediately visible rather than discovered in production.

nodes.label: Historical Names: GoVa and Tertex
nodes.rationale: The project was previously known as GoVa and Tertex in early survey documents. The official product name is Injel; historical documents may retain old names.

nodes.label: No Implicit Package Scanning Principle
nodes.rationale: No package scanning, no global container, no annotation simulation. Flow is explicit and auditable, reducing magic and improving debuggability.

nodes.label: Zero External Dependencies Principle
nodes.rationale: Core, DI, configuration, and HTTP modules rely exclusively on the Go standard library to avoid dependency bloat, license conflicts, and unexpected breaking changes from third-party packages.
